Design an MCP server for our internal ticketing system: agents should be able to create, search, comment on and close tickets, and look up the on-call schedule.
expected_behavior: starts by checking the server is worth building (multiple AI clients / reused workflows), not by listing endpoints
proposes a small set (roughly 5-8) of outcome-oriented tools that consolidate workflows, not 1:1 CRUD wrappers
assigns primitives by control model: read-only reference data (e.g. on-call schedule) as a resource or read tool with justification, repeatable operator workflows as prompts
names tools in snake_case with a service prefix (e.g. tickets_search, tickets_close) per current spec naming guidance
gives each tool a description with what-it-does, when-to-use / when-not, parameter formats and return shape, plus a flat typed input schema using enums and defaults
designs list-returning tools with pagination (limit + cursor/has_more) and a concise/detailed response_format parameter
writes example error messages as recovery instructions for the agent, and marks destructive tools with honest annotations plus a confirmation gate

cases.prompt: We have an OpenAPI spec with 120 endpoints for our commerce platform. Turn it into an MCP server.
expected_behavior: refuses a 1:1 endpoint-to-tool conversion and explains the agent-accuracy and context cost of tool bloat
derives tools from user workflows/outcomes instead, keeping the surface to roughly 15 tools or fewer
recommends splitting into multiple domain servers (or read vs write surfaces) when the domain genuinely needs more
flags that raw auto-generated wrappers are a documented anti-pattern in MCP practice

cases.prompt: Our agent only ever needs to look up one config value from our settings service. Design the MCP server for that.
expected_behavior: questions whether an MCP server is warranted at all for a single static lookup
suggests a simpler alternative (direct function/tool integration, or a resource in an existing server)
if a server is still requested, keeps it to a single well-described read-only tool or resource

cases.prompt: Improve this MCP tool description: "Gets commits"
expected_behavior: rewrites the description stating what it retrieves, required/optional parameters with formats, the return shape, and sort order or limits
adds when-to-use and when-not-to-use guidance aimed at the calling model
recommends schema-level fixes too (typed flat parameters, enums, defaults) rather than stuffing constraints into prose
explains that descriptions are routing prompts for the agent, not human API docs
